summary:
Unforgotten Machines is an interactive application that tells the stories of spacecraft that have explored the Moon, Mars and deep space through the eyes of children. Our goal is to help new generations understand these machines, their missions and their contributions to humanity’s understanding of space in an engaging and accessible way.

For our project, one child researched the machines, another drew their pictures, and a third recorded their stories. We brought their work together with animations and a quiz. Users can select a machine, see its drawing, listen to its story in Turkish or English, and try to identify its mission from three options.

We used artificial intelligence to digitally color the drawings, develop the application and create narrated audio with permission. Our project aims to present space exploration through stories that encourage children’s curiosity and creativity.
details:
Unforgotten Machines is an interactive web application in Turkish and English that introduces children to the stories of machines used in space exploration. Instead of simply listing their names and technical specifications, our project explains their missions through children’s drawings, narration, and animations.

Users can explore ten machines. Each one has a drawing created by a child, an animation related to its mission, and a short audio narration. For example, the Mars helicopter’s rotor spins as it takes off. Users can then play a quiz in which they identify each machine’s mission from three options. The game ends when all ten missions have been identified correctly.

Our goal is to make space exploration engaging and accessible for children. The drawings and narration help make technical information easier to follow, while the game gives users an opportunity to test what they have learned. By offering the experience in both Turkish and English, we hope to reach a wider audience.

Our team members took on different roles. Mustafa researched the machines and their missions. Şevval drew the machines. Abdullah recorded a short narration for each one. In this way, we brought research, art, and storytelling together in a single project.

We developed the application using React, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, built it with Vite, and published it through GitHub Pages. We used artificial intelligence to help develop the application, digitally color the drawings, and create narrated audio using an approved clone of Abdullah’s voice.

When designing the experience, we considered how to make the content easy for children to understand, how to present the machines through large, engaging visuals, and how to help users take an active role in learning. The creative heart of our project is the way it tells the stories of real space missions through children’s own research, drawings, and voices. We hope it encourages users to become curious about space exploration and confident in creating ideas of their own.
